original_question_en: How many edge colors are necessary if every four-vertex clique must contain at least five colors?
answer: The Erdős-Gyarfas function f(n,4,5) equals 5n/6 + o(n) (Banerjee-Bradshaw-Letzter-Pokrovskiy, arXiv:2207.02920).
statement: f(n,4,5) = 5n/6 + o(n), i.e. for every eps > 0 and all large n, |EG n - 5n/6| <= eps*n, where EG n is the least number of colours in an edge colouring of K_n in which every K_4 spans at least five colours (JSP140.FiveSixth JSP140.EG, JSP140.jsp_000140_target).

NEW FILE lean/JSPProblem/Restriction.lean (261 lines, 12 declarations, zero sorry): (1) restrictCol - an edge colouring of K_n restricted along an injection Fin m hookrightarrow Fin n, with mem_edgeFinset_image / mem_edgeFinset_mk_image / colorsOn_restrictCol (a restricted K_4 has EXACTLY the colours it has in K_n) and Admissible.restrict (THE CATALOG CONDITION SURVIVES RESTRICTION); (2) EG_mono - MONOTONICITY of f(n,4,5), m <= n => f(m,4,5) <= f(n,4,5), the elementary fact that had never been formalised in this development; (3) exists_one_mod_six_ge - for every n >= 6 there is m = 1 (mod 6) with n <= m <= n+6, i.e. the extremal residue class is 6-dense; (4) fiveSixthUpper_of_family_const - THE REDUCTION: if for every m = 1 (mod 6) there is an admissible colouring with 6k <= 5(m-1) + 6D for a FIXED constant D, then f(n,4,5) <= 5n/6 + eps*n for every eps > 0 and all n >= max(7, ceil((D+5)/eps)+1), because monotonicity absorbs the five other residue classes and the O(1) slack is absorbed by the eps*n term; (5) fiveSixthUpper_of_extremal_family (D = 0), fiveSixth_of_extremal_family and jsp_000140_main_of_STS_family - THE PRIZE REDUCED TO A SINGLE DESIGN-EXISTENCE HYPOTHESIS: 'for every m = 1 (mod 6) there is an admissible colouring of K_m with 6k = 5(m-1) whose two-edge paths form a Steiner triple system' implies the full catalog statement. Rigidity.lean gained tight_covers and tight_degree: in the extremal case no colour class has an isolated vertex ((twoA c i) union (oneB c i) = univ, i.e. 2a_i + 3b_i = n per colour), with the corollary Main.extremal_no_isolated_vertex. STILL MISSING: only the construction of arXiv:2207.02920 (Bennett-Cushman-Dudek-Pralat), which is PROBABILISTIC (random triangle removal + differential equation method), so there is no explicit colouring in the literature to formalise. Also abandoned this round: the converse reduction (it is false, e.g. n = 7 admits no 5-colouring), explicit constructions with f(n,4,5) <= c*n for c < 1 (merging 1-factorisation classes is structurally impossible, since Cherry.three_mul_paths_le_edges forces k >= 5(n-1)/6), and one-vertex padding with O(1) extra colours (impossible: a K_4 on two old and two new vertices would span only four colours). || PRIOR NOTES === Round 10: build OK, 0 sorry/admit, partial_ok=true, missing_theorems=[jsp_000140_main]. ROUND 10 PROVES THE COMPLETE LOWER HALF OF THE HEADLINE, with the sharp constant 5/6 and no o(n) loss. NEW FILE lean/JSPProblem/Cherry.lean (zero sorry), which discharges the single hypothesis that round 4 had isolated for the whole BCDP22 lower bound (Paths c <= n(n-1)/6, i.e. at most n^2/6 two-edge paths, equivalently: at least two thirds of all edges lie in single-edge components of their colour class). (1) cherry_four_ne - THE K4 CONSTRAINT THROUGH A TWO-EDGE PATH: if a - v - b is a two-edge path of colour i and x is a fourth vertex, then the other four edges s(a,b), s(a,x), s(b,x), s(v,x) of the K4 carry FOUR PAIRWISE DISTINCT COLOURS, none of them i (the K4 carries i twice, must span five colours, and may not carry i a third time). (2) centre_eq_of_leaves / centre_eq_of_leaves' - A PAIR OF LEAVES DETERMINES THE CENTRE: two two-edge paths with the same two leaves coincide. (3) nb_eq_singleton_of_cherry - THE EDGE BETWEEN THE LEAVES IS AN ISOLATED SINGLE EDGE: with j = c s(a,b) one has j != i, nb c j a = {b} and nb c j b = {a}. (4) not_two_centres, leaf_not_centre. (5) cherryEdges / card_cherryEdges / cherryEdges_disjoint - THE COUNTING: the two edges of a two-edge path together with the single edge between its leaves form a three-element set of edges, and the sets belonging to DIFFERENT two-edge paths are PAIRWISE DISJOINT (four cases: two path edges -> not_two_centres; path edge vs leaf edge -> a path edge is never single and a leaf edge always is; two leaf edges -> centre_eq_of_leaves'). (6) Cherry.three_mul_paths_le_edges - THE 5/6 COUNTING LEMMA: 3 * Paths c <= |E(K_n)| = n(n-1)/2, hence Paths c <= n(n-1)/6, unconditionally (six_mul_paths_le, paths_le). (7) Cherry.five_sixth_lower: every admissible k-colouring of K_n (n >= 4) uses at least 5(n-1)/6 colours (5(n-1) <= 6k); EG_ge_five_sixth, EG_ge_five_sixth_real. (8) Cherry.fiveSixthLower_eps: for every eps > 0 and all n >= max(ceil(5/(6 eps)), 4), 5n/6 - eps*n <= f(n,4,5). MAIN RESULTS in Main.lean: fiveSixthLower_eg : FiveSixthLower EG (THE LOWER HALF OF jsp_000140_main, complete) and admissibleLower_eps : AdmissibleLower 1 (the same in the Admissible-colouring language of jsp_000140_target_iff); fiveSixthShape_five_sixth (5n/6 - 5/6 <= f(n,4,5) <= 5n/6 + n/6 + 1 for all n >= 4, the lower side improving from n/12 + 3/4 to the sharp 5/6); fiveSixthShape_sixth_residue' (the SYMMETRIC bound |f - 5n/6| <= n/6 for n >= 5, n != 4 mod 6, which round 9 could not prove); fiveSixth_ge_sixth and fiveSixth_eps_ge_sixth: the catalogue estimate |f(n,4,5) - 5n/6| <= eps*n for EVERY eps >= 1/6 (on n != 4 mod 6), with the sharp constant on both sides (round 9: eps >= 1/4). The classical constant 3/4 of Erdos-Gyarfas (1977) is thereby replaced by the sharp 5/6 of BCDP22. STILL MISSING for jsp_000140_main: only the UPPER half for 0 < eps < 1/6, i.e. an admissible colouring of K_n with 5n/6 + o(n) colours - the BCDP22/JoMu22 construction (1-factorisations of hypergraph matchings); the available constructions are the sum colouring (n colours) and the ghost colouring (n-1 colours for n = 0,2 mod 6), both within O(n) of the target. The residual class n = 4 mod 6 still only has f <= n+1. ROUND 13: build OK, 0 sorry/admit, partial_ok=true, missing_theorems=[jsp_000140_main]. NEW FILE lean/JSPProblem/Rigidity.lean (583 lines, zero sorry): the RIGIDITY OF THE EXTREMAL CASE. pathSet (the three vertices of a two-edge path), cherry_leaf_pair, pathSet_dichotomy, pathSet_sub_inter (THE PACKING LEMMA: two two-edge paths cannot share a two-element vertex set unless they are the same path), pathFinset + card_pathFinset + card_filter_pairIn_le + sum_pairIn_three + sum_card_filter_pairIn (double counting of pairs), IsSTS, tight_pathFinset_is_STS (THE RIGIDITY THEOREM: if the counting lemma 3*Paths c = |E(K_n)| of Cherry.lean is an equality then the pathSets of c form a Steiner triple system on Fin n), tight_attained (the converse: 6*k = 5(n-1) forces tightness, so 'extremal number of colours' <=> 'two-edge paths form an STS'), tight_paths, tight_mod6 (the extremal value is only attainable for n = 1 mod 6), tight_classes_span (in the extremal case every colour class spans V). Main.lean: fiveSixth_at_extremal and extremal_is_STS, so the upper half of jsp_000140_main is exactly the existence of Steiner triple systems of order n = 1 mod 6 with a suitable colouring of the blocks. CORRECTION: arXiv:2207.02920 is by Bennett-Cushman-Dudek-Pralat (not Banerjee-Bradshaw-Letzter-Pokrovskiy) and its construction is PROBABILISTIC (random triangle removal + differential equation method), so the upper half has no explicit colouring to formalise. Also abandoned: the 1-factorisation of K_n is admissible only when 3 does not divide n-1, and an integrality argument extracting 5(n-1)/6 from the o(n) form was formalised, found false and removed.
